# Command

A command palette: a searchable list of every action in the app, in a dialog. Typing filters the commands by label and keywords (ignoring case and accents), the arrow keys move the highlight, and Enter runs the highlighted command. Commands come in labelled groups and show their shortcuts with `Kbd`; when nothing matches it says so. Below 640px it is a full-height bottom sheet, whose search input stays put while the results filter. Above it, the dialog fits its commands, from 32rem up to 40rem, and keeps that width while they filter. A command can lead with an `avatar` or an `icon` and end with an `unread` dot or a `mark`, so a palette that jumps to any chat shows who each one is with and what is new.

```tsx
import { Command } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/command/command";
```

## Example

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useCommandShortcut("mod+k");
<Command
  title="Command palette"
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  items={[
    { label: "Recipes", items: [{ label: "New recipe", onSelect: create, shortcut: ["mod", "n"] }] },
    { label: "Switch theme", onSelect: toggleTheme, keywords: ["dark mode"] },
  ]}
/>

// A palette that jumps to any chat, with each person's avatar and what is unread.
<Command
  title="Go to a chat"
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  items={chats.map((chat) => ({
    label: chat.name,
    onSelect: () => openChat(chat.id),
    avatar: <Avatar name={chat.name} src={chat.picture} alt="" size="xs" idForColor={chat.id} />,
    unread: chat.unread > 0,
    mark: chat.unread > 0 && <Badge>{chat.unread}</Badge>,
  }))}
/>
```

## Usage

Open it with `trigger`, or control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`, usually from `useCommandShortcut`, which opens it on ⌘K (Ctrl+K elsewhere): `import { useCommandShortcut } from "@/lib/ouro/use-command-shortcut"`.

`useCommandShortcut(shortcut = "mod+k")` returns `[open, setOpen]` and toggles `open` on the shortcut anywhere on the page. It takes the keys as `"mod+k"` or `["mod", "k"]`, with Kbd's names: `mod` (⌘ on Apple platforms, Ctrl elsewhere), `cmd`, `ctrl`, `alt` and `shift`. It needs exactly those modifiers, ignores a held key's repeats and prevents the browser's action for that combination. It never fires while an input method is composing text, and in a text field it fires only when the shortcut includes `mod`, `cmd` or `ctrl`, so a shortcut like `"/"` never takes a typed character.

## Use instead when

- Use `Menu` instead for the few actions on one thing, and `Combobox` to pick a value for a form.

## Props

The props the modes share. Type: `CommandProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only, applied to the dialog panel: margins (`mt-8`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | The label of the close button, hidden until it has keyboard focus, so screen-reader users on phones (who have no Escape key) can always close the palette. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` |  | Content for the empty state in place of `emptyLabel`, such as a picture with words: `empty={<Empty icon={<SearchIcon />} title="Nothing matches" />}`. While `loading`, the loading line still shows under it. |
| `emptyLabel` | `string` | `"No results"` | What shows when nothing matches the search. |
| `highlightMatches` | `boolean` |  | Marks the words of the search in each command's label and description, with the theme's colours (the system's mark colours under forced colours). The commands' names stay their plain text. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly CommandEntry[]` |  | The commands: groups (`{ label: "Recipes", items: [...] }`), single commands, or both. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Whether results are on their way: shows `loadingLabel` beside the input, or under the empty state while nothing matches yet ("No chats by that name." over "Searching the directory…"), and announces it politely for the first load of each opening (not again while typing goes on). Set it back to false when the request fails or aborts. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `"Searching…"` | What shows, and is announced, while `loading`. |
| `onQueryChange` | `((query: string, context: { signal: AbortSignal }) => void)` |  | For results from a server: called with the search text on every change, and with the current text (`""` at each opening) whenever the palette opens or swaps between dialog and sheet. The palette then stops filtering `items` itself and shows them as they are, so keep the last results in `items` until new ones arrive. `signal` aborts when a newer query replaces this one or the palette closes: pass it to `fetch`, or drop the response when `signal.aborted`, so a slow earlier response never overwrites a newer one. The app owns the request, and must set `loading` back to false when the request fails or its signal aborts, or "Searching…" stays up. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Type a command or search…"` | The search input's placeholder. |
| `resultsLabel` | `((count: number) => string)` | (count) => count === 1 ? "1 result" : `${count} results` | What screen readers hear, politely and once, when the results for what was typed have settled (not while `loading`, and not for an empty search, whose list is the palette's own). |
| `searchLabel` | `string` | `"Search commands"` | The search input's label for screen readers. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | Names the palette for screen readers; it is not shown. It is always required. |
| `unreadLabel` | `string` | `"Unread"` | What screen readers hear after an `unread` command's label, for other languages. |

## Modes

`CommandProps` is a union: pass the props of exactly one mode. Mixing them is a type error.

### Controlled: `CommandControlledProps`

A controlled Command palette, usually opened by `useCommandShortcut`.

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onOpenChange` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called with `false` when the user closes the palette (Escape, outside press, swipe), and when a command runs. |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` | Whether the palette is open. After a key press it focuses the search input; after a touch or pen tap it focuses itself, so no software keyboard pops up. |

Not in this mode (typed `never`):

- `trigger`: Not with `open`. Remove `open` and `onOpenChange` to let a trigger open the palette.

### With trigger: `CommandWithTriggerProps`

An uncontrolled Command palette: `trigger` opens it.

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` (required) | `ReactElement` | The element that opens the palette, usually a Button: `trigger={<Button>Search</Button>}`. |

Not in this mode (typed `never`):

- `onOpenChange`: Not with `trigger`. Remove `trigger` to control the palette with `open` and `onOpenChange`.
- `open`: Not with `trigger`. Remove `trigger` to control the palette with `open` and `onOpenChange`.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `children`: Not a prop. The commands are `items`: `items={[{ label: "New recipe", onSelect: create }]}`.
- `commands`: Not a prop. The commands are `items`: `items={[{ label: "New recipe", onSelect: create }]}`.
- `isOpen`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `open` with `onOpenChange`: `<Command open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>`.
- `onClose`: Not a prop. `onOpenChange(false)` fires on close: `<Command open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `CommandEntry`

One entry in a Command palette's `items`: a command, or a group of them.

```ts
type CommandEntry = CommandItem | CommandGroup;
```

### `CommandGroup`

A labelled group of commands in a Command palette's `items`.

```ts
interface CommandGroup {
  /** The group's heading: "Recipes". */
  label: string;
  /** The group's commands. */
  items: readonly CommandItem[];
}
```

### `CommandItem`

One command in a Command palette's `items`.

```ts
interface CommandItem {
  /** The command's text, which the search matches. */
  label: string;
  /** Runs the command. The palette closes first. */
  onSelect: () => void;
  /**
   * What tells this command apart from the others, when results change around it: the highlight
   * stays on the command with the same value. Give one when two commands can share a label.
   * @default its label
   */
  value?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * Whether closing the palette after this command runs puts focus back where it was (the
   * trigger). `false` leaves focus where `onSelect` puts it, as a command that opens a
   * conversation and focuses its messages does. @default true
   */
  restoreFocus?: boolean | undefined;
  /**
   * A second line under the label, such as a snippet of a message, which the search matches too.
   */
  description?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * Where to mark the label and the description, as `[start, end]` ranges of each, such as the
   * matches a server found. With these, `highlightMatches` marks nothing else on this command.
   */
  highlight?: { label?: readonly TextRange[] | undefined; description?: readonly TextRange[] | undefined } | undefined;
  /**
   * More words the search matches, which never show: `keywords: ["dark mode"]`.
   */
  keywords?: readonly string[] | undefined;
  /** The keys of the command's shortcut, shown at its end with `Kbd`: `["mod", "n"]`. It does not bind them. */
  shortcut?: readonly string[] | undefined;
  /**
   * A picture before the label, for a person, a chat or a team: a URL, shown in an `<Avatar>`
   * named by the label, or an element to show instead, such as
   * `<Avatar name={person.name} alt="" size="xs" idForColor={person.id} />` for initials in the
   * person's color or a presence dot. Give the element `alt=""`, since the label names it.
   */
  avatar?: string | ReactElement | undefined;
  /**
   * A small icon before the label, in the muted color: a gear for settings, a page for a document.
   * It takes an extra-small avatar's width, so labels line up in a palette that mixes the two.
   * Screen readers skip it; the label names the command. With `avatar`, the avatar shows instead.
   */
  icon?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Something new waits there, as in a chat with unread messages: the label is bold, a dot
   * ends the row, and screen readers hear `unreadLabel` after the label.
   */
  unread?: boolean | undefined;
  /**
   * Something small at the end of the row, before the shortcut: an unread count's `<Badge>`, or
   * words such as "Draft", which show small and muted. It takes the unread dot's place; screen
   * readers still hear `unreadLabel`.
   */
  mark?: ReactNode;
  /** Listed, but cannot be run. */
  disabled?: boolean | undefined;

  /** Not a prop. A command runs `onSelect`: `{ label: "New recipe", onSelect: create }`. (A `MenuItem` is the one that takes `onClick`.) */
  onClick?: { 'Use onSelect: { label: "New recipe", onSelect: create }': never };
}
```
